gen-dafont-eraser-gf-arvo: Arvo's curves stop short of closing, giving the classic serif a dignified, slightly old-fashioned ease on the page. Eraser's bold, uniform strokes sit above it with none of that brush-style swell.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-belgrano: Belgrano reads as a classic serif with open-mouthed curves, traditional and unhurried from the first line. Belgrano keeps that easy rhythm going, while Eraser's bold strokes never swell at a corner.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-biorhyme: BioRhyme brings widely spaced capitals and curves that end like lifted brush strokes. Eraser, cut from one gauge of tubing, supplies the blunt, understated weight that makes that bookish refinement stand out.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-biorhyme-expanded: BioRhyme Expanded opens wide gaps that break each word into single letters, with a clear gap in every e. BioRhyme Expanded stays refined and bookish across a long stretch, while Eraser's bent-tubing heading keeps the same gauge throughout.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-biz-udmincho: Heavy, monoweight skeleton letters mark Eraser as a display face with a quiet, commanding bluntness. BIZ UDMincho follows with a shallow terminal curl and wide gaps, so a larger heading over a smaller body would feel natural.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-copse: Copse lets daylight through every curved opening, literary and classic. Eraser's strokes, pulled like solder through a nozzle, add a thick, understated heading that gives that lightness something solid to lean on.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-david-libre: David Libre reads dignified and refined, its terminals hanging open as the lines move along. And over many lines it stays gentle, while Eraser holds one stroke thickness everywhere above it.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-enriqueta: Literary, with chalk curves that stop well short of closing. Eraser does best as a bold, fixed-width stencil-brush line, while Enriqueta does best at dignified text with a softer touch.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-fenix: Blunt headline, gentle text. Fenix ends its curved strokes before they turn inward, and Eraser, with a ballpoint-pen stroke width, gives that editorial softness a firm, commanding counterweight.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-gentium-plus: Refined is the mood here, with Eraser's bold, unvarying line thickness on top. Gentium Plus gives each c the wide mouth of a pitcher, so a long passage feels open and classic.
